Latest Update: Tri-screen portable monitors aren’t for the faint of heart

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (904 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Living in New York City means making the most of limited space.
  • I’ve experimented with dual-screen laptops in multiple form factors and numerous portable monitors, including ones with projection capabilities.
  • Naturally, a portable monitor with three full-size screens was the next logical step.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Living in New York City means making the most of limited space. As a result, I’m always interested in tools that can boost my productivity at a small desk, in a cramped office, or working on the go.

I’ve experimented with dual-screen laptops in multiple form factors and numerous portable monitors, including ones with projection capabilities. I’ve had particularly good results with dual-screen portable monitors.

Naturally, a portable monitor with three full-size screens was the next logical step.

Recent findings suggest that to get a four-screen (including my laptop’s screen) experience, I tested KYY’s X90G ($360 as of this writing). It’s a portable monitor with three 15.6-inch IPS screens. Each screen has 1920×1080 resolution, its own control buttons, and is specced for up to 400 nits of brightness.

The X90G isn’t the only tri-screen monitor available, but it stood out to me because of its design. Some of the X90G’s rivals place the three displays above the laptop screen, which would require you to look away from the laptop screen repeatedly.

Instead, the X90G places one screen on the left and right sides of the laptop screen and one above the laptop display for a more cohesive—but not completely unified—visual workspace.

The X90G also has better compatibility than its rivals by supporting Linux and Android in addition to Windows and macOS (on systems using an M1 processor or better).

Most laptops should fit in the X90G’s designated area, but many workstations and gaming laptops won’t, since it doesn’t support laptops larger than 17.3 inches.

Let’s get something out of the way: If you hate bezels, a triple-portable-monitor isn’t for you.

Sources indicate that the X90G never felt like one large screen; it always felt like four disparate displays. The screens aren’t perfectly aligned in a row, meaning you sometimes have to move the mouse awkwardly to get from one display to the next.

In a recent development, the gadget’s back panel, where the connected laptop’s screen sits, has a kickstand, so the X90G can be set upright on a tabletop or tilted back. But even with my PC’s lid flush against the monitor’s back panel, parts of the monitor remained visible and distracted me at times.

Sometimes the lit-up screen above my laptop’s lid would inadvertently pull my eyes from my laptop’s display. Worsening matters, I tested the X90G with a 13-inch laptop that, when open, doesn’t cover the opening on the back panel that serves as the monitor’s handle. That means that north of the laptop’s screen was a hole, part of the back panel, a display bezel, and then the extra display.

For some workloads, having four distinct screens is very beneficial. Each of the X90G’s screens supports independent tilting and has its own on-screen display menus, controls, and power buttons. I could keep the screen I was using to write or read an article dimmer while boosting the brightness of the screen displaying an image I was editing, for instance.

The X90G’s design also made it relatively easy to view content on the two side panels and the laptop’s screen simultaneously. This helped me keep things like reports, photos, blogs, spreadsheets, and other documents nearby while conducting research. In these cases, I reserved the northern screen for secondary tasks, like email, chat, or displaying the popular Finnish puppy cam Pentulive.

Sources indicate that I try to keep my workspaces uncluttered to minimize distractions. A tri-screen monitor makes it easier to manage multiple tasks simultaneously but doesn’t allow for the cleanest layout or setup, which presents its own challenges.

It’s also worth noting that you need a decent amount of space to fully extend a triple-portable-monitor setup. The X90G measures about 46 inches across with the side panels flattened out. That’s wider than my desk. You’ll also need some clearance if you want to fold the side panels in toward the laptop more, perhaps for a closer view.

Tri-portable monitors are geared toward people with minimal space who want the flexibility to carry three screens on the go. But these devices are bound to have some bulk. The X90G weighs 6.4 pounds, more than twice the weight of the Dell XPS ultralight laptop I tested it with. That’s a reasonable weight for three displays, but it still inevitably compromises portability.

Alternatively, on days when I could leave the monitor set up and just plug in my laptop, it felt pretty magical to be instantly rewarded with three additional screens by plugging a USB-C cable into my PC.

For someone seeking to maximize small spaces, a three-screen portable monitor sounds reasonable. In practice, though, it’s hard to strike the right balance between portability and screen space with this many displays.

With devices like the X90G, you can quadruple the number of pixels at your disposal. But when I used the X90G, the screens all felt like separate entities, partially because one of them isn’t in line with the laptop’s screen at all. A triple portable monitor can’t moonlight as a larger, unified display, like some dual monitors can.

That mentioned, a tri-screen monitor can do things others can’t, including making it easier to share information with other people.

But if you want a portable monitor for more traditional reasons, such as needing an easily transportable way to get more screen real estate, or if you prefer clear spaces for working, a triple monitor may be overkill, if not overwhelming.

In a recent development, parenting is exhausting. If there’s a new parent in your life, whether it’s your friend who is the new parent of the group or a family member who just had a baby, there are a lot of ways to show some love. Showing up, checking in on how they're surviving, and bringing something that can improve their life are all great ways to support the new parents in your circle.

Industry observers note that there’s a lot of parenting and baby gear out there, and not all of it is created equal. Not all of it will suit what the parents in your life might need, either. This guide is organized into a handful of categories of parenting gadgets, smart home gear, little luxuries, and even food deliveries you can send to their door. All of these are tried and tested by WIRED’s reviewers, many of whom are parents and can confirm the difference it’s made in their lives.

According to recent reports, looking for more baby gear or gift ideas? Don’t miss our gifts for moms and dads or our guide to all the best baby gear.

Updated November 2026: We've added the Calpak Car Organizer, Solly Baby Wrap, and Tubby Todd's gift sets as upcoming gifts to this guide, and a discount code for CookUnity.

Industry observers note that it’s easy to remember to register for things like the car seat and baby clothes. But there are a lot of small gadgets that make parenting a little easier, things that newly introduced parents don’t realize they might love using. Here are some of the favorites from the parents at WIRED.

In a recent development, baby nails are sharp, but it’s also easy to clip their tiny nails too far. The solution? An electric nail trimmer. No more scratches on Mom's and Dad's or baby’s new, beautiful faces. Plus it can be less scary for parents than wielding traditional nail clippers near baby’s tiny fingers.

Industry observers note that this was a gift from a friend that wasn’t actually on my registry, but I used it more than so many things I did register for. Pacifiers fall all the time and get grimy instantly. I kept this portable UV sterilizer hooked to my diaper bag, and loved popping a pacifier in after drops (after wiping it down with a wet wipe first).

The Hatch is my most-used item in the last four years. It was easy to set up on the fly when I came home from the hospital, and I love that I can set up a few scenes in the app to flip through depending on whether I was nursing at three a.m. or putting my son to sleep. The Hatch Baby is now in his room and keeps him asleep each night with its music, while I have the Hatch Restore for myself.

Everyone on TikTok might talk about the MomCozy washer, but the best baby bottle washer WIRED reviewer Nicole Kinning found actually comes from Grownsy. It's quiet, has a deep interior cavity to hold tons of bottle and pump parts, and has multiple modes and combinations you can customize for the perfect cleaning session. It circulates HEPA-filtered air to keep bottles sterile after washing.

According to recent reports, early parenting is survival, and bandwidth to go to the grocery store or cook becomes a hard zero. There’s a reason friends and family often run food trains for new parents. The following food gifts would be a great option to contribute to a food train, and being shippable packages means you can send them to a friend or family member you may live too far from to visit often.

Industry observers note that former WIRED reviewer Matthew Korfhage has tried all kinds of prepared meals, and he says the best one is CookUnity. It’s a ready-to-eat meal delivery service that calls itself a “chef collective”, with regional menus led by regional chefs. Put together a week of meals to send them, or snag them a gift card so they can choose their own. You can also get 50 percent off your first order right now through the end of November with our discount code WIREDCU50.

Hook up your favorite fresh parents with their very own brunch spread. This is a good option to send to their doorstep to feed them for a few days or to bring over in person so they don’t have to worry about having anything prepped. (Great to split with another friend or two for sip and see!) You get to choose up to six bagel flavors, up to three cream cheeses, Nova lox, and can add on more of everything.

Industry observers note that I didn’t put anything fun on my firstborn's registry. I was so overwhelmed with how many must-haves I needed (including an infant baby tub device I never used, but every registry site claimed I'd need). Baby registry websites will constantly tell you that you haven’t added things from every single category their site has deemed important. There are a lot of things parents need, but there are lots of fun things you can gift that aren’t necessities but will still make parenting a little easier, or at least feel like a thoughtful gift.

Shop (The Ultimate Mama + Baby Gift Set).

Sources indicate that one of my favorite things to gift at a baby shower or to a new parent is a nice set of baby-friendly bath and skin-care goods. Sure, a massive bottle of Aveeno will serve them well (it's what you'll usually find in my shower), but this is a fun opportunity to splurge on something nice for them that they will definitely need. I love these sets from Tubby Todd because you have a variety of options to choose from, including just baby or both mom and baby. (Personally, as a pregnant mama, I love the Tubby Todd Belly Oil.).

This was my dream gift as a first-time mom, and I'm finally getting to use one as a second-timer. I loved wrapping my first with a similar (but cheaper) soft wrap in the early months, but the material on the Solly Baby Wrap is much softer and more breathable. The prints are beautiful, and there's cozier double-knit design options if you live in a colder climate.

Sources indicate that if the new mom or dad in your life is struggling with overstimulation, a nice pair of earplugs could go a long way. The Loop Experience 2 cut down some of the volume and noise without completely blocking out sound. Great for epic meltdowns and colicky days without being unaware of what’s going on. I now just carry mine around on my keychain in case I end up somewhere surprisingly loud or forget to plan ahead for a concert.

Where has this organizer been in my four years of parenting? My biggest regret during my son's baby stages was not having a trunk station full of diaper change supplies (and extra clothes). This large car organizer works great for everything from baby gear to keeping your groceries from rolling around and even storing the haphazard amount of toys my son now brings into the car.

It has been revealed that my friend gifted me two of these beautiful muslin swaddle blankets, and they were among my most-used items. I used them to swaddle my summer child without worrying he would melt, and I used them for contact naps so I wouldn’t sweat all over him. It was great for a quick car seat cover or a place to sit him down on some grass—the uses are endless, and there’s a ton of gorgeous colors and prints to gift.

In a recent development, when I had my first child, I fell back into reading to help me stay awake for late-night feeds and contact naps. I read entire series in a matter of days, and I was actually gifted two Kindles for my birthday to help me get off my phone and have a better screen to read on. While my favorite is my Paperwhite, the base Kindle makes for a great gift (and this older version should be on sale soon for Black Friday.).

I’m biased as a smart home reviewer, but the right Wi-Fi–powered gadget could change your life, especially when you’re locked into a contact nap and need to dim the lights without moving. These are a few smart home upgrades I’d recommend gifting to just about anyone, newly introduced parent or not.

I love a digital photo frame, especially as a parent. My camera roll has been stuck in a state of constant overflow since my son was born. I love being able to easily upload photos to my Aura frames to enjoy all the time, and as my son has gotten older, he’s loved seeing them too.

These smart light bulbs from Ikea are super cheap and really easy to control and make routines with. Gift them a set with some remote controls that they can put next to the rocking chair, and they can instantly dim or turn off the lights without needing to get up. They’re Matter-compatible and work with Apple HomeKit, too.

Recent findings suggest that this isn’t technically a smart item, but I’m a big believer that parents who love tea and hot water need to have a double-walled kettle. It’ll keep little hands from getting burned—and big, sleep-deprived hands that forget how hot a kettle can get.

Mom and Dad deserve painless streaming, but there's no hope for that if the remote gets lost. The Google TV Streamer is a sleek system that can also help you locate the remote with a button on the back of the streamer itself, taking one more task off a tired parent's mind.

You probably already gifted the baby something at the baby shower, but if you want to get something for the little one to play with, here are some of our favorite baby toys as WIRED parents.

A good soft book goes a long way with babies who want to chew on every corner, and I like that some of the corners of this Goodnight Moon soft book are reinforced with a chewable texture.

A Jellycat is a kid must-have, and there’s no such thing as too many stuffed animals. Jellycat changes its offerings often, so the one you get could become a treasured, irreplaceable stuffie. (Maybe buy a second if the kid gets really attached!).

I just found my old set of Infantino blocks I had for my son and put them in bags for my second-born-to-be’s toy stash. These large, flexible blocks are easy to stack and safe for baby to stick in their mouths without worrying about choking or sharp corners. This version from Walmart also includes a little activity station to make it easy for your little one to sit and use them.

Lovevery is probably best known for its toy boxes (which are great), but I actually think The Play Gym is one of its best offerings. From months three to seven, this was my kiddo’s absolute favorite place to be. Being in a crowded New York City apartment, having a soft, fun, machine-washable baby space that was easy to move around was invaluable. —Harry Rabinowitz.

If you’re looking to spend a little more on the fresh parents, these smart home and connected gadgets will genuinely improve their everyday life. When I tell you that every parent I’ve hooked on a good robot vacuum comes back to me raving about how much it’s helped them—it’s worth the price of entry. Oregon and Virginia said the firm broke state consumer protection laws.

The attorneys general of Oregon and Virginia have filed lawsuits against SpaceX Super Intelligence, accusing Elon Musk's conglomerate firm of violating state consumer protection laws by allowing users of its Grok AI chatbot to create non-consensual sexually explicit content. The lawsuit alleged that SpaceXSI released Grok's "spicy mode" as a way to "push its lagging product to tens of millions of fresh users," which allowed for the creation of child sexual abuse material (CSAM).

According to recent reports, "This lawsuit is about seeking justice for the millions of Virginians who maintain accounts on X and were misled by the manufacturer's false reassurances that their data and images would be safe on the platform," Jay Jones, Virginia's attorney general, said in a press release. "When xAI allowed Grok's creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritized growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it.".

This morning, X Safety posted that people using Grok for sexually explicit deepfakes "deliberately" violated the Terms of Service, adding that it will "keep testing and adjusting those protections as these abusers change tactics." X Safety also remarked that "protecting children is non-negotiable" and that CSAM "has no place on X or in Grok, and neither do explicit images of real people made without their consent.".

X Safety's post also noted that the tech giant would "take appropriate measures, including actioning accounts and notifying law enforcement," when users circumvent Grok's safeguards to create this type of content. Earlier this year, SpaceXSI filed a lawsuit against one of its users for creating sexual images of real people without their consent.

Beyond Oregon and Virginia, SpaceXSI faced several regulatory investigations and lawsuits in response to owners generating illegal content. The City of Baltimore pursued legal action against Musk's company, claiming that Grok broke the city's Consumer Protection Ordinance; the UK's media authority and the California attorney general launched separate investigations into xAI and Grok.

The Dutch Data Protection Authority is urging consumers not to buy AI-enabled camera glasses, warning that they compromise the privacy of nearby bystanders and risk the safety of their users.

The authority, whose recent statement falls just short of an outright ban, noted that use of the internet-enabled and always-on glasses to record people in public is “almost always prohibited.”.

In a recent development, critics have dubbed these smart wearables as “pervert glasses” for their propensity to be used to video people without their permission, particularly to harass women. While some glasses have warning lights when users are recording, privacy advocates have argued that these alerts are not clear enough. Some people have even made phone apps capable of detecting nearby smart glasses wearers.

Sources indicate that the Dutch data protection authority warned that the glasses also produce wrong results and unsafe results. In one test carried out by the Dutch authority, a pair of unnamed glasses “gave dating advice to an adult who indicated that they are interested in a minor.” The glasses also incorrectly read a medicine label and claimed to have called an ambulance when it had not.

The Dutch government’s advice follows a similar move by the Norwegian government, which in September said it was considering a ban on camera-enabled devices.

Hands-on: Baseus’ new PicoGo Pro USB-C charger is clever, cute, and on sale

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (632 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5google

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • USB-C chargers are pretty standardized at this point, but there’s a fun new trend of adding displays to your power brick that I’ve been very much enjoying, and the new PicoGo Pro from Baseus is a great example with three ports, optimized charging, and a cute little character to top it off – and for Black Friday, it’s pretty deeply discounted, too.
  • The Baseus PicoGo Pro (AH22) is a 100W, 3-port USB-C charger designed to top off your laptop, phone, and/or tablet, even all at the same time.
  • It has been revealed that using GaN tech, PicoGo Pro is very compact at about 2 inches tall and a little over an inch wide.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

USB-C chargers are pretty standardized at this point, but there’s a fun new trend of adding displays to your power brick that I’ve been very much enjoying, and the new PicoGo Pro from Baseus is a great example with three ports, optimized charging, and a cute little character to top it off – and for Black Friday, it’s pretty deeply discounted, too.

The Baseus PicoGo Pro (AH22) is a 100W, 3-port USB-C charger designed to top off your laptop, phone, and/or tablet, even all at the same time. For anyone who travels often or just has a lot of devices on hand, chargers like this are a must. Having something you don’t have to think twice about when it comes to charging rates is just so nice, and these have come a long way, too.

It has been revealed that using GaN tech, PicoGo Pro is very compact at about 2 inches tall and a little over an inch wide. I remember having single-port chargers that could barely fast-charge my phone that were twice this size just a few years ago. GaN just absolutely rules, and Baseus is using a special version that reduces heat and improves efficiency.

But the two reasons I really like this charger aren’t strictly to do with GaN.

The first is the built-in display. Again, that’s a trend throughout the industry. Anker has several chargers out with built-in displays as the company helped to really make this popular – the Anker Prime 160W brick is really similar to PicoGo Pro (at a higher price), and it’s the only I’ve been using for months before trying out this Baseus model.

Baseus has a cute little animated character that accompanies your charging, with little eyes when the charger isn’t active and some fun animations to show your charging rate in real-time. Neat! You can “press” the button to move through the UI and even see the specific charging rate of each connected device. You’ll also see that the brick can recognize the device you have plugged in, though Android devices just show a generic “SAMSUNG” or whatever brand you plug in – Anker, again, had a similar set of features in a brick released earlier in 2026, but some of those features were iPhone-only, and that brick was only a 1-port, 45W charger anyway.

But, like that Anker brick, Baseus supports “smart” charging that adjusts to your device. Plugging in a Galaxy Z Fold 8 that was around 65% full, I saw the brick adjust its charging speed to tailor to the phone, initially going up to full speed before settling down around 28W~. You can manually adjust this with “Turbo” or “Gentle” modes, the former maxing out the charging rate and the latter settling in around 15W for a slower charge. That flexibility is great because it means you can adjust the charging rate to what you need in that moment. Full-speed for a quick top-off on a busy day, slower charging overnight to preserve battery health.

Baseus isn’t doing much new here, though the GaN tech mentioned earlier is enhanced by some architecture and algorithm adjustments the firm has made behind the scenes, but it’s a really good implementation.

Beyond that, it’s also priced pretty well.

Recent findings suggest that baseus PicoGo Pro’s full price is $59.99, but you’ll probably rarely see it there. Technically, today is its launch date, and it’s already down by over 30% at $39.70 for Black Friday. Value-wise, this one is hard to beat.

#3019. What the green flashing light on your Roku remote is telling you

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (681 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

What the green flashing light on your Roku remote is telling you

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (681 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A remote that won't cooperate can put your streaming intends on hold.
  • Regardless of what you think of Fox's takeover, Roku is still an undeniable force in smart TVs.
  • Sources indicate that one of the reasons for the platform's popularity is its simplicity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A remote that won't cooperate can put your streaming intends on hold. Here's how to work out what's wrong and get back to the content you love.

Regardless of what you think of Fox's takeover, Roku is still an undeniable force in smart TVs. The firm's products are an easy choice when looking for the best streaming devices, and of course a number of TVs now ship with Roku OS built in, most notably models from TCL and Hisense. Roku is the main game in town for brands that are not using Google TV, Fire TV or their own proprietary software.

Sources indicate that one of the reasons for the platform's popularity is its simplicity. That said, there are times when the platform can be a little obtuse, mysterious blinking lights on the remote being a prime example. It's easy to assume that means a problem — but what, exactly?

If you're dealing with a flashing green LED on your Roku remote, the fix could be very straightforward, simply requiring fresh batteries or a recharge, depending on the model. In some circumstances, however, you may need to do more or replace your remote entirely. Hopefully you've already got the Roku app on your phone as a backup, which can save you in a pinch when your remote is on the fritz.

Sources indicate that as we just suggested, one reason for the light may be that your remote's batteries are low. If that's the case, swapping in new batteries (if there's no built-in one) should rapidly solve the problem. If you find this is happening too frequently, though, it may be because you're using rechargeable batteries. Alkalines are costlier in the long run — but Roku does recommend them for remotes with replaceable batteries. You can check battery levels in advance by navigating to Settings > Remotes & devices > Remotes > Your remote > About.

You'll also see this light if you're trying to set up a replacement remote. Using your old one or the Roku app, you may need to head to Settings > Remotes & devices > Add devices > Remote > Continue to complete the process. You'll definitely see green flashing if you trigger a remote's physical pairing controls, which is done by holding a dedicated button or the Back and Home buttons simultaneously for five seconds.

It has been revealed that there's no need to be worried unless the light is flashing rapidly after re-pairing. If that's going on, it's a sign that your remote is probably broken and needs to be replaced. Note that you can also buy third-party remotes; sticking with one of Roku's official options should get you better support and features. Whatever you choose, verify that it's going to be compatible with your particular TV or streamer.

If you've run through all of the above steps short of replacing your remote, one remaining option is to restart it. If it uses replaceable batteries, take them out, then press any two buttons before reinserting the batteries, negative sides first. If it uses a built-in battery, hold down its physical pairing controls (see the last section) for 20 seconds.

At this point, there's not much else you can try short of clearing the cache on your Roku or updating or rebooting your Roku device, or you could learn how to reset your Roku. Be warned that if you try a reset, you'll have to reconfigure everything as if it were right out of the box. It's also unlikely to solve a green light glitch, since as we've established, that's normally related to battery levels or pairing, not buggy software.

If worst comes to worst, you may be stuck using your phone for control. One pro tip, though — you don't always have to use the Roku app. If your setup supports AirPlay from iPhone or MacBook to your TV or screen mirroring on Roku with your Android phone, you can often cut to the chase with whatever audio or video it is you're trying to play.

A Tower Records shop in the RyuBo department store in Naha, Okinawa.

Tower Records Japan will start shipping online orders again from Monday. A breach last week exposed about 11 million customer records, it stated. The music retailer gave the update on Sunday evening in its notice on the incident. Its online store, Tower Records Online, stays shut for now. Its marketplace has no date to reopen.

Tower Records spotted the unauthorised access at about 5:10pm on Thursday, 19 November, and took the store offline. Its investigation then found that customer data had leaked.

The leak covers members of its Tower Records Members scheme, including people who left within the past three years. The company broke it down into three groups:.

A hashed password cannot be read as it stands, the company stated. No credit card data leaked. As of Saturday it had found no misuse of the data. It warned customers about emails pretending to come from Tower Records. It is contacting affected customers by email.

Tower Records has not said who was behind the attack or how they got in.

Recent findings suggest that tower Records is the latest Japanese retailer to disclose a breach, Bloomberg reported. A day earlier, the online fashion retailer Zozo reported a separate leak. It noted attackers got into KARTE, a marketing platform run by the Japanese firm Plaid, on 13 November.

In a recent development, the Zozo leak covers about 15.2 million ZOZOTOWN shoppers and 13.9 million WEAR app people. Most records hold member IDs, ages and genders. For about 47,000 shoppers they also hold emails and phone numbers. No passwords leaked, Zozo said. Marui Group, which uses the same platform, reported a similar incident, Bloomberg reported.

Japan has already stepped up cyber warnings after a run of leaks. Bloomberg named older IT systems as a weakness and stated the PHP2Shell flaws hit Japan hard. In the US, Chase, Visa and Mastercard confirmed vendor hacks last week.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cybersecurity giant CrowdStrike has agreed to buy Zscaler in a $43.9 billion all-stock deal, the companies confirmed Monday.

CrowdStrike and Zscaler remarked that the deal will create the “largest single addressable market” for cybersecurity, which will enable the companies to better position themselves for the AI era.

Zscaler is a San Jose, California-based tech tech giant that provides cloud cybersecurity products to about 8,000 enterprise companies. The company offers zero-trust technology, a security feature that requires employees to authenticate each and every time they access an internal system or resource. The aim is to protect against hackers from stealing credentials and using them to gain unfettered access to a company’s network.

In a recent development, crowdStrike, which secures the computers, laptops, phones, and other devices connected to a company’s network, noted the deal will unite its endpoint protection software with Zscaler’s zero-trust platform to better defend their customers against data breaches. By combining the two products, CrowdStrike and Zscaler say that they can offer “superior protection” to their customers.

In remarks on Monday, the companies stated that the acquisition will help customers safely adopt AI.

The deal, which is subject to regulatory approval, is expected to close around this time next year.

#3014. F1 in Las Vegas: You've never seen an F1 race like this before

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1888 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

F1 in Las Vegas: You've never seen an F1 race like this before

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1888 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Las Vegas welcomed Formula 1 to its streets this past weekend.
  • The Vegas street circuit—the one that looks like an upside-down pig—is an extreme outlier on the calendar.
  • But the 17 turns are mostly all low speed, so there’s no risk of seeing the cars driving demoralizingly slowly through corners that are supposed to test one’s mettle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Las Vegas welcomed Formula 1 to its streets this past weekend. And for the first time since the event’s inception in 2023, the Grand Prix delivered on a long-promised spectacle. The racing was closer to an IndyCar oval race than anything F1 fans will have seen since slipstreaming was the order of the day at places like Monza and Hockenheim, back when humans were still landing on the Moon and downforce had yet to fundamentally change racing.

The Vegas street circuit—the one that looks like an upside-down pig—is an extreme outlier on the calendar. It has plenty of long straights, so this year’s cars still suffer from energy starvation throughout the lap, as the inadequate size of their lithium-ion hybrid batteries means they become depleted very quickly, leaving the cars on just over half power with their V6 engines operating without the benefit of the hybrid’s electric motor.

But the 17 turns are mostly all low speed, so there’s no risk of seeing the cars driving demoralizingly slowly through corners that are supposed to test one’s mettle.

Sources indicate that and because it takes place at night, in the desert, in November, it’s cold—much, much colder than anywhere else the sport will visit all year. This coming weekend in the Middle East, track temperatures may well exceed 122° F (50° C ); on Saturday night in Nevada the track was a mere 59° F (15° C). Combined with the concrete streets, that spells low grip, but there is an added benefit—virtually no tire wear or overheating.

It has been revealed that and finally, there’s the slipstream. This was far more powerful than in years past, thanks to the newly introduced aerodynamic regulations. We saw this play out in qualifying, which took place on Friday night, when Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli snatched pole position by being the last man on track and benefiting as the cars ahead cleared the air out of his way. Conversely, the Ferrari duo of Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc had a torrid time by not working together—a preview for the following night, as we’ll see….

Antonelli’s pole was promptly forgotten, though, as the new World Champion would only start sixth due to a grid penalty for using an engine component outside his allowance.

In a recent development, because of the penalty, Red Bull’s Max Verstappen was on pole, with Mercedes’ George Russell next to him. To say there is little love lost between these two drivers would be to undersell the depths of animosity in that relationship. This was evident in FP3, when the pair clashed on track in what looked like a repeat of the Verstappen/Liam Lawson incident in Mexico. This time, no penalties were handed out.

“He does this week in, week out with many drivers, and everybody accepts it, and I’m not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they’re bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody’s got to stand up to that guy,” Russell stated on Friday. That set up the prospect of a lap 1, turn 1 coming together, but instead the start of the race was remarkably clean. But not boring.

Recent findings suggest that within a lap, Russell had passed Verstappen for the lead on a straight, before the Red Bull reclaimed the position going into turn 17 on the last corner. This set the tone for things to come, with the Mercedes repeatedly getting past the Red Bull at turn 14, only for Verstappen to regain the lead through sheer commitment, taking back his lead in the corners.

Don’t be tempted to call this yo-yo racing; it was nothing like the races we saw early in the season, when everyone was still trying to understand their hybrid deployment and regeneration strategies. Like an oval race, knowing when to try to move up through the pack was vital; choosing it wrong meant losing multiple positions, not just one. But like an oval, it was also possible to work one’s way up through the pack.

Recent findings suggest that the second Red Bull of Isack Hadjar looked more competitive than at any other time this year, and, had the two teammates worked together, they might have been able to leapfrog each other to break free of the pack—a tactic we see used to good effect on oval races. Whether Verstappen’s temperament would allow him to let his teammate past even temporarily remains unknown (I have my doubts), but Red Bull never tried it, instead ordering Hadjar to hold position, leaving him vulnerable to attack from behind. His day was ruined when his front wing exploded on lap 25, dropping him from third to dead last.

So Verstappen never broke free of the chasing pack, with five or six cars covered by as little as 2.5 seconds for much of the time.

Again and again Russell took the lead briefly but lost it again to Verstappen, who worried over the radio that the Mercedes team had figured out his strategy and was going to be able to defeat it on the last lap.

“I think in the beginning we had the deployment immediately correct, but of course, people are learning and watching what you’re doing. At one point, I couldn’t get back into the lead before the start-finish line, so I just—that’s why I asked the question,” Verstappen remarked after the race. “But I think we had it set up well, and it was just a crazy amount of fighting. The slipstream was so major that you—it was just impossible to drive off, and it was just crazy how many people were just following you.”.

Industry observers note that but Mercedes fumbled. George Russell crashed into a barrier on lap 47—probably as he ran over a piece of Hadjar’s broken wing, preventing him from braking in time. And Antonelli blew his own chance when, instead of charging his battery for that last-lap, last-corner pass, he accidentally drained it entirely. The team that claimed the 2026 Constructors’ championship last time out in Mexico had to settle for another weekend off the podium.

Recent findings suggest that verstappen claimed his 75th win, one he said was more like Mario Kart than any of the previous 74. McLaren’s Lando Norris was just 0.64 seconds behind him, with the other McLaren of Oscar Piastri a similar gap behind his teammate. The orange pair worked well together and took home a significant bounty of points in their fight with Ferrari for second place in the constructor’s championship as a result.

Industry observers note that ferrari’s Friday was already being called a disaster, as the two red cars couldn’t make it into the third and final qualifying session. Had they worked together to tow each other, this might have been possible. But things are far from harmonious at Ferrari between their two very closely matched drivers, with plenty of fireworks recently in Mexico City.

According to recent reports, during the race, things got worse. The cars stratified themselves according to performance, which meant teammates running together often. Early on, Hamilton and Leclerc kept it mostly clean, although Hamilton earned a 10-second penalty when he went off track to avoid Norris and Leclerc, dropping him to 14th at the time. With safety cars, strategy, and that strong tow, Hamilton clawed his way back up the running order and was again in front of Leclerc by lap 34.

In a recent development, four laps later, Leclerc tried to pass Hamilton—despite being specifically told by his team five corners earlier to hold position. Leclerc misjudged it, like he did in Monza and Mexico, and the cars made contact, dropping Hamilton to 10th. The race stewards clearly apportioned blame to Leclerc, handing him a 10-second penalty. Hamilton eventually finished seventh, Leclerc 10th.

Recent findings suggest that leclerc appears desperate to show the team he’s better than the seven-time champion it hired to race alongside him, but time and again his efforts end badly, costing the team points instead. Team boss Fred Vasseur had evidently read Leclerc part one of the riot act before the media pen—the pallid, tear-stained face of the Monegasque driver was that of a man who looked like he knew he really screwed up this time. Having signed a massive multiyear contract, his position with the team is presumably safe. But were I Vasseur, one of Ferrari’s reserve drivers would be getting a call to get ready to replace him for the weekend in Qatar.

Like Leclerc and Hamilton, Russell has been writing checks about Verstappen that his racing hasn’t cashed, and in the post-race interview, Verstappen had simply epic levels of disrespect for the other driver.

Recent findings suggest that “The thing is, he speaks a lot next to the track, and honestly, you know, for me, it doesn’t really bother me because he’s so far below my level that it doesn’t really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that, you know? So it doesn’t bother me,” Verstappen said. “And today, karma is a bitch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening, so I was like, ‘Fantastic, my day is only getting better.’ And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete.”.

In a recent development, so many unique circumstances went into making this particular Las Vegas Grand Prix as exciting as it was, and there’s little chance the next two rounds, which both take place in the Middle East, will see similar conditions. But F1 can take something away from this race to make future seasons better, and it’s to do with the tires.

It all goes back to the 2010 Canadian Grand Prix. Like this year in Vegas, Canada 2010 was chaotic. The weather was cold, the traction zones were covered in a low-grip surface to combat the tarmac disintegration seen in the years before, and the action was unpredictable as each team tried to figure out on the fly how best to adapt.

Industry observers note that F1’s powers that be saw this, and when they awarded Pirelli a sole supplier contract for tires the following year, they instructed the company to make race tires that would cause the same effect. Of course, it hasn’t ever worked out like that. Canada 2010 was a one-off and caught the teams off guard. But running the same Pirelli tires race after race, everyone promptly figured out the optimal strategy, leaving little room for chaos.

It has been revealed that and the Pirelli tires, while better than they once were, are still difficult to drive on. Pirelli mandates high minimum pressures out of fear of tire failures, and next week in Qatar has told teams they cannot run a set for more than 27 laps. As we frequently see in races, tires that stay within their temperature window while running in clean air can quickly overheat when following another car. In the wake of a car ahead, the following car has less downforce and slides more in the corners, which puts more heat into the tires, and the trailing car falls behind. Pirelli makes the tires that F1 asks for, but after this weekend’s race, it’s time for the sport to ask for something different.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that tesla owners know all about subscription pricing when it comes to their vehicles. The company's Tesla Full Self-Driving (Supervised) feature requires a subscription of $99 per month.

Of course, Tesla owners don't need FSD in order to drive their vehicles. They can drive the car that they own without paying the monthly fee. But what if a subscription was required?

That's the case with Tesla's new Cybercab.

In a recent development, in order to use the $29,990 Cybercab at all, owners will be required to pay $299 per month for a subscription. Without the subscription, the Cybercab won't move.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk did share on his social media platform X that he thought the subscription was too pricey.

"The monthly fee is too high," Musk posted. "Should match the cost of Tesla FSD and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month." It has been revealed that it should be noted that the monthly fee can change at any time. And while Musk noted he'd like to lower the price, Tesla could also raise it.

In addition to the required $299-a-month subscription just to use the Cybercab, there are other restrictive terms that buyers must agree to.

Sources indicate that for example, Cybercab owners cannot put wraps on their vehicle, tint the windows, or change the wheels unless the work is approved by and done through Tesla. If owners make those changes without Tesla, the company can suspend a Cybercab owner's subscription, effectively bricking their car.

In addition, subscriptions can be temporarily suspended without refund if a Cybercab owner operates the vehicle in an improper or unsafe manner.

Another rule, at least for now, is that a Cybercab can only be used for personal use. Tesla Cybercabs cannot be used for rentals or with apps like Uber or DoorDash.

The Tesla Cybercab is also geofenced, meaning it currently can only be used in approved areas of Texas. Attempting to use the car outside of the approved areas can result in operation of the vehicle being "technologically prevented.".

The pros and cons of wearing your Fitbit around your ankle

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (612 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An ankle-worn Fitbit can catch steps your wrist misses, though some health metrics may suffer.
  • It's frustrating when you've finished your daily walk, but Fitbit didn't catch all the steps because it couldn't recognize them.
  • Some have found a way around this by wearing their Fitbit on their ankle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An ankle-worn Fitbit can catch steps your wrist misses, though some health metrics may suffer.

It's frustrating when you've finished your daily walk, but Fitbit didn't catch all the steps because it couldn't recognize them. Or when you've pushed a stroller, held the treadmill rails or worked at a walking desk, and discovered that limited arm movement makes your brisk walk look unimpressive in the app. Out of all the Fitbit hacks, tricks and tips out there, this basic problem has persisted for many people.

Some have found a way around this by wearing their Fitbit on their ankle. It may seem like a strange fix, but having the motion sensor closer to your feet can help. Fitbit devices measure more than just steps, but they depend on arm movement to gather data. While Google often assumes you're wearing the Fitbit on your wrist, activities with limited arm movement mean your health data may not be accurate.

In a recent development, fitbit trackers use accelerometers to recognize movement patterns associated with walking, but a wrist-worn sensor can miss steps when your arms remain still. Google acknowledges that pushing a stroller or shopping cart can lead to missed steps. Walking pads create similar issues when you're typing at your desk rather than allowing your arms to swing. In these cases, an ankle-worn Fitbit measures leg movement directly. It also keeps your wrist free if you dislike wearing watches or if your workplace bans wrist-wear.

There's some evidence behind the idea. In a 2025 study, 11 healthy adults walked with a single-point cane or two-wheeled walker while wearing Fitbit Inspire 3 trackers on their wrists, hips and ankles. The hip and ankle placements had a combined average step-count error of 1.5 percent, while wrist readings were substantially less reliable. It's a significant difference, but keep in mind this small study involved assisted walking, not daily activities.

Industry observers note that the concept isn't all that novel, either. The Moov Now supported ankle wear back in 2015 and was specifically designed for it, unlike current Fitbits.

According to recent reports, wearing a Fitbit on your ankle doesn't automatically translate to what you're doing. In a test, a Fitbit Versa 4 logged 1,510 steps during a 30-minute stationary bike session when worn on the ankle, versus 180 when the same tracker was worn on the wrist. Pedaling an exercise bike isn't the same as steps, and you're likely more interested in monitoring heart-rate. Also, the tracker did fail to record sleep during a nighttime ankle test.

Speaking of heart-rate, Fitbit's optical sensors measure blood-volume changes through the skin to estimate your pulse, and Google recommends wearing the device snugly against your wrist. The company hasn't established comparable accuracy for ankle placement, where fit and sensor contact differ.

Sources indicate that A recent experiment summed up the debate. The ankle-worn Fitbit Air picked up walking pad steps the wrist-worn Pixel Watch 4 missed while the reviewer was typing. Conversely, one walk produced a heart-rate peak of 182 beats per minute on the ankle-worn Fitbit, compared to 129 bpm maximum measured on the wrist. Four more walks failed to repeat the spike, so it's not conclusive proof ankle readings are always incorrect.

Finally, Fitbit looks fine on the ankle, but standard wristbands may be too short. Aftermarket ankle straps cost extra and a loose tracker can rub uncomfortably against socks or shoes. And of course, checking notifications is difficult. For those who want to keep their wrist free, the Fitbit Inspire 3 also has an official clothing clip option, but this mode does not include heart-rate tracking, Active Zone Minutes or automatic exercise tracking.

  • “I spoke to them, let me put it that way … And I convinced them,” the president told CNBC.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A close ally of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, President Donald Trump reportedly dialed into an Nvidia board meeting to push for the ousted CEO’s return, Semafor reported on Monday. Trump got his way, as Nvidia revealed Huang’s reinstatement shortly afterward.

“I spoke to them, let me put it that way … And I convinced them,” the president told CNBC.

Huang was forced to step down from his role as CEO, which he held for 33 years, after news broke that he had affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees, including a direct report.

“President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board. We have to protect our geniuses,” White House communications director Steven Cheung told Semafor.

The president took to his social media app, Truth Social, to remark that “the United States government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to national security.”.

Industry observers note that according to Nvidia’s press release about Huang’s reinstatement as CEO and president, the company claimed that “the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”.

In a recent development, while Trump has declared that Huang “did absolutely nothing wrong,” many government officials aren’t buying the president’s point of view. Huang is still expected to testify in closed-door conversations with three committees of the House of Representatives on December 1. He is also slated to appear before the Senate Banking Committee to testify publicly, though that hearing has not been scheduled yet.

Industry observers note that “People say, is it a threat to have him? No, it’s a threat to lose him,” Trump remarked to CNBC.

Trump has maintained this position through the scandal, even denying that he was ever told about Huang’s relationship with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang (no relation). The Upcoming York Times reported, on the contrary, that Trump’s secretary of state and national security adviser Marco Rubio briefed him aboard Air Force One in May.

Earlier this spring, Rubio also supervised the drafting of a memo that circulated among top policymakers, warning that Alice Huang was spying for China’s Ministry of State Security.

It has been revealed that sierra, the AI customer service company led by Bret Taylor, is raising $1.75B at a $30B valuation, it confirmed on Monday. Greenoaks and Lightspeed Venture Partners are leading the round.

Industry observers note that the valuation is almost double the $15.8B Sierra was worth in May, when it raised $950M. All of its previous lead investors, including Benchmark, Sequoia and Tiger Global, are investing again.

Sierra builds AI agents that answer customers’ calls and messages for large companies. It says its annual recurring revenue passed $400M in October, just over two and a half years after launch. Almost half of the Fortune 50 are customers, it says.

Sierra charges for outcomes, such as a resolved problem or a paid insurance claim, rather than per seat or per token, and Zendesk is moving the same way. Insurer Guardian recently handed it 1 million dental calls a year, and its agents can now take card payments through Stripe.

Taylor, who also chairs OpenAI’s board, co-founded Sierra with former Google executive Clay Bavor. In a blog post, the pair addressed fears of an AI bubble.

It has been revealed that “We’re seeing some of the oldest, most regulated companies in the world deploy AI the fastest,” they wrote. They pointed to last week’s record Anthropic IPO as a sign of how fast AI is moving.

Sources indicate that competition in AI customer service is heating up. In June, Salesforce agreed to buy support-AI firm Fin for $3.6B.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Michelle Branch has a question for Gen Z: Are you happy now?

More than two decades after its release, the singer-songwriter's 2003 breakup anthem "Are You Happy Now?" is finding a new audience on TikTok, thanks to a particularly memorable needle drop in Netflix's buzzy teen horror drama The Body. And for millennials who grew up screaming along to the song in their bedrooms, the sudden resurgence feels like a long-overdue moment of recognition — and another painful reminder that we're all old AF.

Welcome to the Michelle Branch renaissance. We've been expecting you.

Sources indicate that the song appears in the third episode of The Body, a psychological horror series set at a Catholic girls' school in 2004, where a dance team initiation spirals into a supernatural panic. The show's early-aughts setting provides plenty of opportunities for nostalgic needle drops, with a soundtrack featuring Kelly Clarkson, Ciara, Kylie Minogue, and No Doubt. But Branch's angsty pop-rock hit gets one of the show's most memorable musical moments.

Industry observers note that during a church service, Elise puts on a convincing display of demonic possession, collapsing as the song builds toward its explosive chorus. The juxtaposition of religious imagery, teenage hysteria, and Branch's soaring vocals makes for a scene practically engineered to go viral.

And that's exactly what's happening on social media.

Sources indicate that originally released in 2003 as the lead single from Branch's supremely underrated sophomore album, Hotel Paper, "Are You Happy Now?" became one of the defining songs of the early-2000s pop-rock boom. With its crunchy guitars, emotionally charged vocals, and deliciously confrontational chorus, the track captured a particular kind of teenage heartbreak — the kind that demands to be felt at full volume.

Sources indicate that it was a time when young women like Branch, Avril Lavigne, and Vanessa Carlton were helping shape the sound of mainstream pop, bringing guitars, messy emotions, and confessional songwriting to a generation of listeners. They embraced teenage melodrama, not shied away from it.

According to recent reports, now, more than 20 years later, that sound is resonating with a upcoming generation. Just look at the comments on the song's YouTube music video, where the top comment asks, "Who's here after The Body?".

On TikTok, younger listeners are discovering the cathartic power of Branch's early-aughts angst. One user declared it the upcoming background song to their life, while another thanked The Body for introducing them to this "cunty asf song." Others are already looking to expand their musical horizons. "I've been obsessed with this song since The Body," one user wrote, asking for recommendations for artists with a similar sound.

But the nostalgia goes beyond the music itself. One TikToker lamented being born in 2004 instead of getting to experience the year as a teenager, adding, "God I'm SO jealous of millennials." Another praised the show's music supervisor with a particularly heartfelt blessing: "Whoever put this soundtrack together, I hope both sides of your pillow are cold cause wow, you get it.".

The resurgence is part of a familiar pattern in which television and social media introduce younger audiences to older music. Kate Bush's "Running Up That Hill" famously experienced a massive revival after appearing in Stranger Things, while TikTok has repeatedly turned decades-old tracks into contemporary hits.

Industry observers note that what makes "Are You Happy Now?" particularly well-suited to this moment is that its emotional intensity never really went out of style. The song's combination of wounded pride, anger, and catharsis translates just as easily to a TikTok edit as it did to a burned CD in 2003.

It has been revealed that for Gen Z, it might be a new discovery. For millennials, it's confirmation of something we've known all along: Michelle Branch was always that girl.

For a generation that grew up online, the early 2000s have become something of a cultural fantasy. From Y2K fashion and digital cameras to wired headphones and the resurgence of pop-rock, Gen Z has embraced the aesthetics of a time when the internet still seemed full of possibility. More recently, the "millennial optimism" trend has romanticized the late 2000s and early 2010s, when Tumblr aesthetics, twee fashion, and earnest indie music dominated the internet. It's quite the turnaround for a generation that once made mocking millennial cringe something of a pastime.

But millennial optimism is about more than nostalgia for a particular aesthetic. It's a longing for a time when the future seemed brighter, when hope and sincerity felt less embarrassing, and when pop culture wasn't quite so steeped in irony. Of course, the past wasn't nearly as carefree as nostalgia might suggest. Still, there's something appealing about the emotional earnestness of that era, especially its music.

It has been revealed that and while "Are You Happy Now?" might not exactly embody millennial optimism, its resurgence taps into that same longing for a seemingly simpler cultural moment. The platforms might have changed how we discover music, but the desire to scream along to a song that understands exactly how you feel hasn't changed much at all.

Next up: Justice for Carlton's "White Houses.".

It’s also removing Google Assistant from smart speakers and displays.

Sources indicate that it's been a long-time coming, but Google is finally preparing to retire the Nest app early next year. On January 25, 2027, the firm will sunset the software. You'll need to download the newer Google Home app if you'd still like to continue controlling your Nest devices remotely and receive notifications from them. Then, on August 2, the company will retire Google Assistant on smart speakers and displays, with Gemini replacing the older tech for voice controls.

Sources indicate that "The Nest app rolled out over 15 years ago, and home technology has changed a lot since then," Google claims of the decision. "To give every Nest user Google's latest security protections and most advanced cyber defenses, plus new features from Gemini, we're bringing all Nest devices together in the Google Home app." Additionally, the company argues its new infrastructure is faster, more reliable and more secure. Another benefit of the migration is that you'll be able to watch live footage from your Nest cameras on more of your other devices, including TVs and smartwatches.

According to recent reports, if you've yet to migrate your Nest devices to the Google Home app, the manufacturer claims your existing settings and schedules will transfer over automatically. The only thing you need to manually move over are any custom clips you might have saved over the years. You can do this by visiting the Nest website before January 25 and clicking the "Download all" button. Google says it will automatically migrate Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions to its newer Google Home Premium package. "You will receive an email closer to the date of transfer detailing your subscription information," the company adds.

Recent findings suggest that google bought Nest more than a decade ago, and while the brand was a visible part of the search giant's portfolio in the early years after the acquisition, it gradually dropped the Nest name in favor of its own. As for Google Assistant, the writing for it has been on the wall for a while now. Earlier this year, Google removed Assistant from Android phones and tablets, as well as Wear OS and other related devices.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that monday morning, Jensen Huang returned as CEO of Nvidia, after resigning the position following news of multiple affairs, including one with a subordinate and one with a woman tied to Chinese intelligence services.
  • In a recent development, still, tech leaders should be clear-eyed about all the problems likely to come with Huang’s reinstatement.
  • Most importantly, serious questions remain about how Nvidia chips were smuggled into China, and how much Nvidia knew about it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s safe to say no one expected this.

Recent findings suggest that monday morning, Jensen Huang returned as CEO of Nvidia, after resigning the position following news of multiple affairs, including one with a subordinate and one with a woman tied to Chinese intelligence services. With so much of the AI industry built on top of Nvidia’s AI infrastructure, Huang’s departure looked like an imminent threat to the business — and the mood on his return has been ecstatic. Share prices are rocketing back up, particularly for neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius, and the Nasdaq rose 7% on the news.

In a recent development, still, tech leaders should be clear-eyed about all the problems likely to come with Huang’s reinstatement. President Trump is already telling reporters that the U.S. government found no national security concerns resulting from the affair, but the broader national security concerns aren’t so easy to dismiss, and Trump’s involvement may do more harm than good for Nvidia and its partners. This isn’t the end of the problems caused by Huang’s affairs; it’s likely just the beginning.

Most importantly, serious questions remain about how Nvidia chips were smuggled into China, and how much Nvidia knew about it. Among Jensen Huang’s defenders, it’s become common to question whether Alice Huang was really a spy, but it’s clear that a lot of restricted chips were flowing into China through her organization. Just this weekend, The Latest York Times reported sustained contact between Alice Huang and a member of China’s Ministry of State Security during the same period she was having an affair with Jensen Huang.

Sources indicate that with Democrats in control of Congress, including investigative bodies like the House Oversight Committee, there are plenty of ways to force the glitch. Nvidia’s role in violating U.S. export controls would likely have been the subject of prolonged uncomfortable investigation, whether Huang returned or not. But with him back in the CEO’s seat, there will be a lot more riding on any revelations that come up — and any upcoming revelations will damage Nvidia as a firm alongside Huang himself.

Then there are the questions raised by Trump’s intervention. It’s unprecedented in American history for a sitting president to intervene to clear a CEO accused of being a national security risk. Simply pressing the Department of Justice to exonerate Huang would have been a scandal, but calling the Nvidia board goes significantly further. Huang has already donated $25 million to Trump’s ballroom project, so it’s easy to make the case that Trump was intervening on behalf of a donor, setting national security risks aside for his personal benefit.

Recent findings suggest that all of this is happening just as Democrats retake Congress, with all of its associated investigative powers. Even if they can’t fire Huang or remove Trump, there are lots of uncomfortable questions that are still unanswered. Was there any Department of Justice inquiry into whether Huang had committed a crime, or did Trump make the call on his own? Did the intelligence services make any official assessment that could be subpoenaed into the congressional record? Investigating Democrats will be particularly interested in Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who oversees export controls and retains significant financial ties to the industry through his firm, Cantor Fitzgerald.

According to recent reports, if all of this sounds exhausting, you’re getting a sense of what the next year will be like for anyone following national news. Congress will keep a steady drip of embarrassing revelations, milking as much political juice as possible out of Huang and everyone associated with him. Trump will keep lashing out, often making things worse for everyone involved. (Trump’s statement to CBS, which defends Huang in racist terms while also accusing him of treason, is an early taste.) It’s going to be ugly and sad, and the most successful tech firm of the last decade will be right at the center of it.

According to recent reports, I have to assume that this was the scenario the board was concerned about when it decided to remove Huang two weeks ago. Since then, the cost of removing him has gone up: an open letter from Nvidia’s employees and partners, a tanking stock market, and, ultimately, direct intervention from the president of the United States.

But nothing has lowered the cost of keeping Huang, and the ugly scenario the board foresaw earlier this month is still very much in place. We’re about to see it come to life.

COP31 ends in failure as countries split over fossil fuels, climate finance

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (988 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • ANTALYA, Turkey—By the time the United Nations COP31 climate talks ended Sunday afternoon, the conference center resembled a going-out-of-business sale at a pawnshop for broken dreams.
  • As cleaning crews cleared away the debris left by more than 100,000 participants, Murat Kurum, president of the Conference of the Parties and Turkey’s minister of environment, urbanization, and climate change, tried to tie together disparate parts of a draft climate deal with a shiny ribbon of multilateralism.
  • It has been revealed that for the first time since 2009, the conference ended without consensus on a cover decision, the concluding statement that typically signals global solidarity on how to confront the worsening climate crisis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

ANTALYA, Turkey—By the time the United Nations COP31 climate talks ended Sunday afternoon, the conference center resembled a going-out-of-business sale at a pawnshop for broken dreams.

As cleaning crews cleared away the debris left by more than 100,000 participants, Murat Kurum, president of the Conference of the Parties and Turkey’s minister of environment, urbanization, and climate change, tried to tie together disparate parts of a draft climate deal with a shiny ribbon of multilateralism.

Many countries were not buying it.

It has been revealed that for the first time since 2009, the conference ended without consensus on a cover decision, the concluding statement that typically signals global solidarity on how to confront the worsening climate crisis. Countries did adopt several decisions, including a program to help workers and communities transition away from fossil fuels, and a proposal to assess progress on climate adaptation.

The failure to agree on an overarching conference statement reflected deep divisions over whether the agreement should mention fossil fuels and carbon capture, as well as how much climate financing developed countries should provide to developing nations hit by costly climate disasters.

The European Union, as well as several Latin American countries and Pacific Island states, said they would not accept the proposed text from the conference leaders.

Cover decisions at the annual conferences usually focus on upcoming steps or language that could reinforce international efforts to slow global warming. A central aim at this meeting was to set quantifiable but voluntary global goals for the widespread electrification of economies, and to increase funding from developed countries to help developing countries adapt to climate impacts.

In 2022, the UN conference in Egypt agreed to establish a loss and damage fund to help vulnerable countries pay for irreversible climate impacts. A year later in Dubai, delegates from more than 190 countries agreed, for the first time, that a “just and orderly” transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems is needed to slow global warming.

It has been revealed that since then, international collaboration on climate issues has declined amid increased conflict, rising oil and gas prices and economic insecurity. The talks in Turkey ran two days beyond the scheduled end without reaching broad agreement on potential next steps, an outcome that won’t kill the global effort but is widely viewed as a serious setback.

But compromise for the sake of consensus is not enough, remarked Kathy Jetn̄il-Kijiner, a climate envoy for the Marshall Islands Ministry of the Environment.

“We will not be forced to accept false solutions,” she said. “We will not compromise our future to benefit fossil fuel interests.” As written, she added, the Antalya Pact undermines her country’s security and threatens its future.

In a recent development, “People are dying, seas are rising, and ecosystems are collapsing,” Jetn̄il-Kijiner remarked. “Are we so divorced from reality that we take backward steps, even as overshoot threatens to overtake us? To accept this deal would be a betrayal to the Marshallese people.”.

It’s not the first time Pacific Island nations threatened by rising seas have objected to the outcome at one of the United Nations’ annual conferences. During the 2023 UN talks in Dubai, a final text was adopted even though a delegation representing 39 small island developing states objected because they were still outside the plenary meeting, trying to coordinate their position.

Industry observers note that but in Antalya, the divide ran much deeper. The economically powerful and politically influential European Union, representing 28 member countries, also rejected the proposed agreement.

Ireland’s climate, energy, and environment minister, Darragh O’Brien, stated the European countries formally objected to the cover decision because it fell short of what the global climate crisis demands.

“We will not endorse a decision that does not even mention fossil fuels, the key driver of climate change, and not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuels,” mentioned O’Brien, speaking on behalf of the EU during Ireland’s rotating presidency.

Egypt and Brazil, hosts of the UN climate talks in 2023 and 2025, also criticized the text proposed by COP31 president Kurum of Turkey and Chris Bowen of Australia, president of the conference negotiations.

Liliam Beatris Chagas de Moura, director for climate at Brazil’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, noted she was disappointed that this year’s conference did not sustain the momentum from last year’s talks in her country.

Mohammad Ayoub, a climate negotiator with the Saudi Arabian energy ministry, remarked the 22-member League of Arab States supported the proposed Antalya Pact. He criticized developed countries for using up most of the global carbon budget, the amount of fossil fuels that can be burned without overheating the planet, and then asking developing countries to give up the very energy sources that fueled their own growth.

Ayoub condemned some countries’ opposition to including references to carbon dioxide removal and carbon capture and storage in the pact, calling their resistance to those technologies unscientific.

Carbon capture and storage are not close to being deployed fast enough “to keep 1.5 degrees within reach,” he said, referring to the long-term goal of limiting the average global temperature increase established by the 2015 Paris climate agreement.

“We believe that climate change requires all solutions on the table, and that countries select from these solutions depending on their national circumstances.”.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres said he was “deeply disappointed” that the talks ended without consensus on an overarching agreement.

“But this setback does not change the facts,” he said. “Fossil fuels are driving the climate crisis. We can’t put out the fire while pouring fuel on it.”.

Sources indicate that bob Berwyn is an Austria-based reporter who has covered climate science and international climate policy for more than a decade. Previously, he reported on the environment, endangered species, and public lands for several Colorado newspapers, and also worked as editor and assistant editor at community newspapers in the Colorado Rockies.

This story originally appeared on Inside Climate News.

What crucial features should you look for in a home security camera?

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that when you're shopping for the best home gadgets, a lot of decisions tend to be based purely on budget or personal preferences.
  • Recent findings suggest that with security cameras, though, your decisions can be deadly serious.
  • In a recent development, I've tested or owned a number of security cameras for more than a decade.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that when you're shopping for the best home gadgets, a lot of decisions tend to be based purely on budget or personal preferences. No one needs an RGB lamp, for example, and an accessory that works with Google Home will usually function just as well paired with Amazon Alexa or Apple Home. There's a reason why Apple's new HomeView and HomePod mini 2 come in multiple colors — form might matter as much as function to some customers.

Recent findings suggest that with security cameras, though, your decisions can be deadly serious. If a camera fails when you need it most, the results could be vandalism, property theft or yes, someone getting hurt or killed. Even your choice of doorbell camera matters, given the number of porch pirates out there.

In a recent development, I've tested or owned a number of security cameras for more than a decade. At this point, I'm very familiar with the requirements for a great one. Just be warned that you may not be able to check off every item on your wishlist, especially if your goal is a security system that can operate 24/7, even when power or Wi-Fi goes out.

According to recent reports, when it comes to a camera's sensor, resolution isn't as important as you might think. 4K is nice to have — but more important than that is the device's night vision and field of view. The wider the view, the more a camera can potentially capture, with 180 degrees being ideal. As for night vision, you don't necessarily need color, but a sensor should be sensitive and sharp enough to clearly discern faces when little to no ambient lighting is available. I wouldn't buy a camera with less than 2K/1080p resolution and recommend searching online for real-world sample images.

Outdoor cameras should be fully water- and dust-resistant, with a rating of IP68 or better. Ensure the device's temperature limits are suitable to the climate you live in. Both wired and battery-powered cameras are potentially viable outside, but be aware that without a compatible solar panel, you're going to have to recharge batteries every six to 12 months at best. Actual runtime depends on factors like motion activity, signal strength and how often you check live feeds. You should be able to go at least a month between charges.

In a recent development, AI-based recognition of people, packages, animals and/or vehicles is sometimes crucial to avoiding a flood of generic motion alerts. That technology is often tied to both internet access and a subscription, though, so you might want to focus on models that handle recognition on-device at no extra charge. As subscription features go, cloud recording is more valuable. While local recording to an SD card is cheaper, it won't help you much if a thief steals or destroys your equipment.

Third-party platform support may also be vital. If you've already got one of Amazon's Echo Show or Fire TV devices in your home, for example, it only makes sense to pick up cameras with Alexa integration. You'll be able to check activity without pulling out your phone and set up camera-linked automations — for instance, triggering lights when motion is detected and you're away from home. Apple and Google offer similar hardware and software options. Note, however, that Apple Home can only be controlled using first-party hardware. That might make it a no-go if anyone in your home relies on an Android phone.

Recent findings suggest that if you're away often enough that someone might break in when power or internet access is down, search for battery-equipped cameras with cellular and SD card backup. This combination is going to be expensive, even before you factor in a monthly data initiative, but it's the only bulletproof solution. Alternately, you might invest in a Wi-Fi router with cellular backup and a whole-home battery solution, but the battery component alone will probably cost you thousands of dollars.

The one remaining question is whether it's worth paying for professional monitoring. That's more subjective. Based on my own experience, the cost probably isn't worth it. All monitoring crews can do is call emergency services for you, and you might as well call the police yourself if you've received an intruder notification. There might be some value if you're regularly out of town for days or weeks at a time, as you're probably preoccupied, and you can't just dial 911 (or your regional equivalent) to reach the police in your hometown.
